observer-console.name: observer-console-0
observer-console.alt: Observer Console during the night: Hα frames of the Helix Nebula reviewed in heat colours, with guiding running, the sky conditions and safety at GO.
observer-console.caption: One dense frame to observe by hand: target, telescope, camera, filters, rotator, focuser and dome, with guiding, sky conditions and safety alongside, and every frame reviewed as it lands.

observer-console.name: observer-console-1
observer-console.alt: Observer Console in Queue mode, preparing a 2×2 mosaic of the Helix Nebula with the rotator at 25°.
observer-console.caption: Queue exposures and build mosaics on the fly: Arcsecond lays out the tiles, the filters and the rotator angle, then runs them for you.

night-scheduler.name: night-scheduler-0
night-scheduler.alt: Night Scheduler running tonight's sequence on NGC 253, with its airmass curve, the steps of the sequence, and a sidebar of targets of every kind.
night-scheduler.caption: Build a night as a sequence of steps, from opening the dome to closing it, press Run, and come back in the morning. Every step is recorded.

transient-alerts.name: transient-alerts-0
transient-alerts.alt: ToO Policies verdicts listing alerts from Swift, SVOM, Fermi, Einstein Probe, IceCube, LVK and ZTF, beside the runs they triggered.
transient-alerts.caption: Listen to NASA's GCN and Fink's ZTF streams: every alert is scored against your policies, and the observable ones can interrupt the night to be observed at once.

transient-alerts.name: transient-alerts-1
transient-alerts.alt: ToO Policies: interruption policies, notifying or interrupting per mission, beside the observation series they run.
transient-alerts.caption: Decide which missions notify and which interrupt, within which limits of altitude, Sun, Moon and error box, and what the telescope observes when they do.

safety-configuration.name: safety-configuration-0
safety-configuration.alt: Safety Configuration listing the safety procedures beside the default condition sets on weather, night bounds, mount limits and Sun avoidance.
safety-configuration.caption: Combine condition sets on weather, Sun, Moon and mount limits with your own procedures: close the dome, park the mount, cover the optics, cut the power.

safety-configuration.name: safety-configuration-1
safety-configuration.alt: Safety Configuration decisions log, listing a day of GO and NOGO changes with the conditions that triggered them and the procedures they ran.
safety-configuration.caption: Arcsecond evaluates your conditions continuously and keeps every GO/NOGO change, with what triggered it and what was done about it.

calibrations-manager.name: calibrations-manager-0
calibrations-manager.alt: Calibration Manager with bias templates, the plans combining biases and darks, and their daily and weekly schedules.
calibrations-manager.caption: Describe your biases and darks once, combine them into plans and schedule them: Arcsecond takes the frames and files them in dedicated datasets.

calibrations-manager.name: calibrations-manager-1
calibrations-manager.alt: Calibration Manager browsing a past run of darks, with its frames and their previews.
calibrations-manager.caption: Browse every calibration series ever taken, with its frames, previews, night and dataset, ready for your pipelines.

equipment-registry.name: equipment-registry-0
equipment-registry.alt: Equipments Registry with all the Alpaca devices of the observatory connected and the T100 telescope selected, showing its pointing and state.
equipment-registry.caption: Register your ASCOM Alpaca devices once, then connect, monitor and drive each of them: telescope, camera, dome, filter wheel, focuser, rotator and more.

equipment-registry.name: equipment-registry-1
equipment-registry.alt: Equipments Registry with the science camera selected, showing its last exposure of 47 Tucanae, its statistics and the exposure controls.
equipment-registry.caption: Expose, cool and inspect right from the registry: each camera shows its last frame, its statistics and its settings.

equipment-registry.name: equipment-registry-2
equipment-registry.alt: Equipments Registry with the all-sky camera selected, showing its live fisheye image of the night sky.
equipment-registry.caption: USB, network and all-sky cameras join the registry through the Arcsecond CLI's live-image proxy: streamed live, and recorded all night long.

polar-alignment.name: polar-alignment-0
polar-alignment.alt: Polar Alignment overview of the T100 mount: its last measurement with knob guidance and a pole plot, and the history of three measurements.
polar-alignment.caption: Measure how far your polar axis sits from the pole, with its uncertainty: Arcsecond tells you which knob to turn, by how much, and follows it over time.

night-explorer.name: night-explorer-0
night-explorer.caption: Our flagship tool, the Night Explorer (a.k.a. iObserve), the best decision-making tool for planning and scheduling observations. Used by many astronomers worldwide.

fdc-editor.name: fdc-editor-0
fdc-editor.alt: FOV Simulator & Finding Charts Editor screenshot
fdc-editor.caption: Our Finding Chart Editor is a powerful way to prepare detailed and highly customized finding charts, with custom overlays from large instruments or even your own.

transit-browser.name: transit-browser-0
transit-browser.caption: Our Transit Browser has been extended! It allows to browse the currently accessible transits for exoplanets, at a given time and location, as well as non-regular transits and other transiting objects.

transient-sky.name: transient-sky-0
transient-sky.alt: Transient Sky: a sky map and a table of events from Swift, SVOM, Fermi, Einstein Probe, IceCube, LVK, TNS and ZTF, each judged observable or not from the telescope, one event selected.
transient-sky.caption: Every transient of the last day on one sky map, from NASA's GCN, TNS and Fink's ZTF stream. Each is judged from your telescope against your ToO policies; select one to import it as a target.

target-lists.name: target-lists-0
target-lists.caption: The Target Lists are a simple way to organize and manage your observing targets. They can be used to plan observations, track progress, and share with colleagues.

data-browser.name: data-browser-0
data-browser.alt: Data Browser listing the datasets on an observatory NAS, with the frames of NGC 5128 and their previews.
data-browser.caption: Browse every dataset, on Arcsecond Cloud or on your own storage (here an SMB NAS of the observatory), with headers and previews, organised night by night.

observations-browser.name: observations-browser-0
observations-browser.alt: Observations Browser in Per Night mode, listing six nights of observations with their targets, start times, durations and previews.
observations-browser.caption: Every observation of every night, extracted from your data or recorded by the Control Room, grouped by night log.

observations-browser.name: observations-browser-1
observations-browser.alt: Observations Browser in Per Target mode, with NGC 253 selected and its observations over three nights.
observations-browser.caption: Follow each target across the nights: how often, with which telescope, for how long. Arcsecond keeps the list up to date by itself.

data-viewer.name: data-viewer-0
data-viewer.alt: Data Viewer showing a FITS image of Centaurus A in heat colours, with its statistics, a close-up of a star and the FITS header.
data-viewer.caption: Open any FITS or XISF frame right in the browser: scales, colour maps, statistics, a close-up under the cursor and the full header. Nothing to install.

virtual-filesystem.name: virtual-filesystem-0
virtual-filesystem.caption: The Virtual Filesystem is a tool dedicated for people uploading their data to Arcsecond Cloud Storage using our Python CLI/Module. It reproduces the local filesystem structure, allowing to recover your familiar organisation in the cloud.

data-sharing.name: data-sharing-0
data-sharing.caption: Data Distribution & Sharing is a dedicated tool to organise datasets into packages, and share them privately to people inside or outside Arcsecond.

observatory-schedule.name: observatory-schedule-0
observatory-schedule.alt: Observatory Schedule showing a month of nights, maintenance and meetings, with a night log selected and its observations and previews.
observatory-schedule.caption: One calendar for the whole observatory: nights fill in by themselves from your data, beside maintenance, meetings and visitors, per telescope and per person.

observatory-map.name: observatory-map-0
observatory-map.alt: Observatory Map of Cerro Arcsecond: two domes with their telescopes and equipment, the control building with its servers and network, and the NAS.
observatory-map.caption: Arcsecond draws your observatory from its registry: domes, telescopes, equipment, buildings, computers, software and storage, and how they are linked. Then make it yours.

data-storages.name: data-storages-0
data-storages.alt: Data Storages with the observatory NAS attached over SMB as the default destination, and the log of its latest push.
data-storages.caption: Attach your own NAS, SMB share, S3 bucket or SFTP server: Arcsecond.local pushes every new file and database backup there, and logs every push.

observatory-settings.name: observatory-settings-0
observatory-settings.alt: Observatory Settings composing the file names of new frames from telescope, target, filter, exposure and date blocks, with example names.
observatory-settings.caption: Compose the name of every frame your observatory takes from simple blocks: telescope, target, filter, exposure, date and more.

observatory-settings.name: observatory-settings-1
observatory-settings.alt: Observatory Settings with the observatory's SMTP server configured to send invitations, password resets and notifications.
observatory-settings.caption: Plug in your observatory's SMTP server: invitations, password resets and notifications leave from your own domain.
